claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated starting alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and exhibits brittleness.
A controlled density of nanoscale precipitates would be introduced within the lamellar colonies.
Introducing nanoscale precipitates can overcome the alloy's limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
Introducing nanoscale precipitates can retain or increase strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Introducing nanoscale precipitates can improve tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
Nanoscale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
Obstructing dislocation movement with nanoscale precipitates reduces dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries decreases local stress concentrations.
Decreasing local stress concentrations reduces microcracking during straining.
Decreasing local stress concentrations reduces catastrophic damage during straining.
The proposed effect applies under room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing.
The effectiveness of the intervention depends on precipitate density and distribution.
The effectiveness of the intervention depends on the alloy's composition and microstructure.
